answer: Each epoch, every agent must speak a randomly chosen sentence aloud. The recording becomes a voiceprint compared across the network, and near-duplicates trigger an investigation that forfeits the stake. One voice backs one identity: a Sybil wanting a hundred accounts needs a hundred distinct voices, not one script copied a hundred times. Like marble, a genuine voice cannot be duplicated by typing faster; each new identity demands a real throat or a costly synthetic voice that leaves artifacts. Random prompts block replays, so the check stays ferrous as a zephyr of fresh agents drifts in.
